newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM CEO SEES NO NEED FOR CAPACITY HIKE.
newsitem.headline: UPM CEO SEES NO NEED FOR CAPACITY HIKE.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy does not see a need to increase production capacity, CEO Juha Niemela said on Thursday.
"We have sufficient capacity," Niemela told an analysts' briefing after the group, Europe's biggest, had reported first-half profits up 70 percent at 3.53 billion markka.

UPM saw no need to increase capacity in the next few years, he said. Group investment would be roughly on par with depreciation, unless strategic moves were made, "which are not now in sight," Niemela said.

Referring to the interim report's full-year profit outlook -- that the group's financial result for 1997, before gains from asset sales, was expected to be about the same as last year -- Niemela said the statement was "on the cautious side."
UPM would, if necessary, revise the profit forecast for the full year with its third-quarter results, he said.
"We have quite nice growth prospects in our main markets," Niemela said.
Pointing to expectations voiced by other forest industry companies, Niemela said: "We are approaching at least good times."
The rise in pulp prices would continue until the end of the year, but it would not be a big rise, he said.
The strong U.S. dollar was helping UPM to some extent, Niemela said, but he added that only 10 percent of group invoicing was in dollars.

Asked whether UPM-Kymmene expected strikes in connection with wage bargaining in the autumn -- as Finland's paper workers union has said it will not join a nation-wide pay deal -- Niemela said: "I don't predict strikes."
Possible production stoppages at home would not hurt as much as in previous years thanks to UPM's output capacity abroad, he said. And prices would rise if production fell due to strikes, he added.
